What Are Custom Powder Coating Colours?

Custom powder coating colours are shades matched to your specification rather than picked from a stock range. The powder is sprayed on electrostatically and cured in an oven, so the colour becomes part of a hard, even finish instead of a thin layer of paint.

Most requests fall into three groups. The first is a standard shade from our powder colour range. The second is RAL colour matching, where you give us a RAL number. The third is a colour match to a sample, where you send us a chip, swatch or small part. Each group changes how we source the powder and how we confirm the result with you. A custom powder coat colour is only as good as its reference, so a clear specification saves time.

Custom powder coat colour is only half of the decision. Sheen levels decide how that colour looks once it is on the part. Gloss powder coating is smooth and bright, matte powder coating cuts glare, and satin powder coating sits in between. The same shade can read very differently in each, so we talk through sheen before we order the powder.
How We Match and Apply Custom Powder Coating Colours

We confirm your colour reference, prepare the metal, apply the powder electrostatically, cure it at 180–200 °C and inspect the result against your sample. Each step protects the colour match and the finish quality from the first brief to the final check.

items: Colour brief. Send a RAL number, a RAL colour chart reference, a brand specification or physical colour samples. Samples are best, because screens and printed charts rarely show the true shade. This is where custom colour matching starts.
Powder selection. We check the powder coating colour chart and our supplier range for your shade and finish. If a colour must be ordered in, we confirm the timing with you before work starts.

Surface preparation. Clean metal holds colour evenly. We degrease, remove rust and scale, and pretreat the part where needed, as described on our [surface preparation](/services/surface-preparation) page.
Masking. We plug threads and bores and cover contact points so your custom powder coat colour stays only where you want it.
Spray and cure. The powder is applied electrostatically, then cured in the oven at 180–200 °C. The heat melts the powder and bonds the pigment into one continuous film.
Inspection. We compare the finished custom powder coating colours with your reference, check coverage and thickness, and look for defects before packing.

blocks.text: Some finishes need an extra step. Candy colours and certain effect powders are often built as a two-coat finish, with a coloured base followed by a second layer. This adds time, so we explain it when we quote. For repeat orders, we record the powder and colour code to support batch colour consistency on later runs of your custom powder coating colours. Whether your custom powder coating colours are in stock changes the timing, so we check availability early.
Which Parts and Metals Can We Colour?

We apply custom powder coating colours to steel and aluminum parts, from small brackets to large fabricated frames. The part must withstand oven curing, so we review each item before quoting. See our [capabilities](/capabilities) page for size and weight limits.

Typical work includes railings, gates, bollards, machine guards, equipment housings and frames. Powder coating for fabricated parts is a large share of what we do, and one consistent colour across welded assemblies is often the main requirement. Galvanized and cast metals can need extra checks because trapped gases may affect the surface, so tell us the material when you ask for a quote. Send photos with your request so we can check size, weight and masking needs early. Every custom powder coat colour we apply is matched to the metal as well as the specification.

Parts that live outdoors also need the right powder. UV-resistant powder coating holds its colour better in sunlight, which matters for fences, outdoor furniture and building metalwork. For an outdoor-durable finish on exterior products, see our [architectural powder coating](/services/architectural-coatings) service, or read our guide to [outdoor furniture finishes](/post/powder-coating-outdoor-furniture-weatherproof-finishes).
Finish Options for Your Colour Choice

You can pair any custom powder coat colour with a finish type: gloss, satin, matte, textured, metallic, candy or clear coat. The finish changes how the colour looks, feels and wears, so it is worth choosing both together. These powder coating finishes give you plenty of room to match a design.

items: Gloss and high-gloss finish. A smooth, reflective surface that is easy to wipe clean.
Satin and low-gloss finish. A softer sheen that shows fewer fingerprints and marks.
Matte. A flat, modern look with the least glare.
Textured powder coating. A wrinkle finish or hammertone finish adds pattern, and an anti-slip textured finish improves grip. Texture also hides surface imperfections such as light weld marks.
Metallic powder coat. Our custom colour powder coating can include silver, bronze and copper metallics that add depth and sparkle.
Candy powder coating. A translucent custom powder coat colour over a base that gives rich colour depth.
Clear coat powder coating. A transparent top layer that protects metallic and candy effects.

blocks.text: Choosing between metallic shades? Our [metallic finishes guide](/post/metallic-finishes-explained-powder-coating) explains the differences, and our [RAL colour guide](/post/powder-coating-color-matching-ral) shows how RAL numbers translate to powder.
How We Check Colour and Finish Quality

We check your custom powder coat colour against your reference, measure film thickness and test adhesion before parts leave the shop. Our quality steps are outlined on our [certification](/certification) page, and test reports are available on request. Ask us about them when your project specification requires proof.

Where a job calls for it, test methods include ASTM D3359 for adhesion, ASTM D7091 for dry film thickness and ASTM B117 for salt spray resistance. Our certification is held through the Absolute Bureau of Certification. A custom powder coating colour is only useful if it stays attached and even, so we test the finish as well as the shade.
Fade resistance depends on the powder chemistry and the pigment. Bright reds and oranges fade faster outdoors than neutral tones, so we ask where the part will be used before recommending a powder.

Who Uses Custom Colour Finishes

Fabricators, welding shops, contractors and manufacturers order custom powder coating colours most often, because their parts must match a client's brand or a building's design. Consistent custom powder coating colours matter as much as the shade itself.

[Metal fabricators and welding shops](/industries/metal-fabricators-welding-shops) send us weldments that must match a customer's colour. [Contractors and construction](/industries/contractors-construction) teams order railings, gates and site metalwork in colours chosen by designers. Branded colour matching and corporate colour finishes are common for equipment makers. For larger production runs, see our [industrial powder coating](/services/industrial-powder-coating) service, or browse all of our [powder coating services](/services). Whatever your sector, we handle custom powder coating colours the same way: confirm the reference, match the powder and check the result.
Custom Colour and Finish FAQs

These answers cover colour matching, sheen, fading, clear coats and repeat orders for custom powder coating colours. Each answer is specific to this service, so you can decide quickly what to send us.

blocks.q: Can you match a colour from a physical sample?
blocks.a: Yes. Send a chip, swatch or small part and we will work to match it to the closest available powder. We tell you before work starts if the match is not close enough.

blocks.q: What is the difference between gloss, satin and matte?
blocks.a: Sheen. Gloss is shiny and smooth, satin is softer and matte is flat. Sheen changes the look, while protection comes from the powder type and the preparation.

blocks.q: Will custom powder coating colours fade outdoors?
blocks.a: Any colour can fade over time, but UV-resistant powders slow it. Bright reds and oranges fade faster than neutrals, so tell us the exposure and we will suggest a suitable powder.

blocks.q: Do metallic and candy finishes need a clear coat?
blocks.a: Often, yes. A clear coat protects the effect and improves durability. We confirm whether your colour needs one when we prepare the quote.

blocks.q: Can you keep the same colour across repeat orders?
blocks.a: Yes. We record the powder and colour code for each job, which supports batch colour consistency for your custom powder coating colours. Tell us if a tight match matters, because powder batches can vary slightly.

blocks.q: What do I need to send for a custom colour quote?
blocks.a: Send the part size, quantity, finish and a colour reference such as a RAL number or sample. A photo of the part helps us confirm masking and preparation. This lets us price your custom powder coating colours accurately.
